newsitem.title: UK: Allied Domecq gains, H1 results in line.
newsitem.headline: Allied Domecq gains, H1 results in line.

text.p: Shares in Allied Domecq Plc rose in pre-market trading on Tuesday as first-half results came in as expected and the stock continued to be lifted by bid and merger speculation, dealers said.

The stock, which jumped 18p on Monday as the planned merger between Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc sparked bid speculation across the industry, was up 11p at 457-1/2 by 0710 GMT in volume of 230,000 shares.
"If it was just the results, the stock probably wouldn't have been much changed," said one head of equity trading.
"They are talking about a recovery in the second half but the press is full of talk of consolidation and people just won't be looking to sell this stock."
Dealers said it was comment on the Grand Met-Guinness deal that had the major impact on the stock.
The influential Finacial Times Lex column said wholesale consolidation in the industry had become inevitable after Monday's merger announcement.
It said the enlarged GMG would "gain cheaper product distribution, a far broaded portfolio and thus an edge both in growing its sales and squeezing better prices."
By 0731 GMT Allied shares were up 14-1/2p at 461, not far from its year's high of 470p set on March 19.
Guinness was down 6p at 596-1/2 after Monday's surge and Grand Met was down 5p at 586-1/2.

The Beefeater gin-to-Dunkin' Donuts group said pre-tax profit was static at 317 million stg in the six months ended February 28, though at comparable exchange rates profits would have risen three percent.
Analysts had expected pre-tax profits in a range from 304 million stg to 325 million. Allied held its dividend at 9.44p, compared with an expected dividend of 9.63p.
It said there had been improved results from some but not all its core spirits brands and further growth in leading pub brands.

Second-half trading was in line with expectations, Allied said, with benefits to come from higher U.S. spirits sales after last year's destocking, though for the year as a whole there would be an estimated 28 million stg impact from the strength of sterling.
